title: Sealed audit log pipeline: cryptographic chaining, WORM export, and verification CLI
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: Build a tamper-evident audit export pipeline that (1) cryptographically chains admin/access/config events as they are emitted, (2) produces signed, time-indexed manifests, and (3) ships immutable exports to WORM-compliant storage with automated verification tools for auditors and support. This ticket covers the server-side signer, the export producer, manifest format, WORM sink writer, and a lightweight verification CLI used by internal compliance and by customers (for Private deployments).

Background: Current audit logs are stored in append logs and S3 lifecycle buckets but lack an end-to-end integrity guarantee and a signed manifest that proves no silent deletion or trimming occurred. Regulators require both retention controls and demonstrable tamper-evidence for admin actions and config changes.

Scope:
- Event-level hashing and chaining (Merkle or hash-chain) at the ingestion boundary for admin/action/access/config-change events.
- Periodic signed manifests containing chunk-level root hashes, sequence ranges, and KMS-backed signatures.
- Export writer that writes manifest + payloads to a WORM policy S3 bucket (or on-prem equivalent) with retention metadata.
- Verification CLI that downloads manifest(s), validates signatures via KMS public keys, and re-computes hashes over downloaded payloads to detect tampering. CLI must support an offline mode for air-gapped Private installs.
- Integration with audit retention settings (per-customer residency + retention period) and automatic evidence generation for reporting automation.

Non-goals: Full UI for retention settings (handled by PM tickets), analytics on logs, and long-term archive retrieval UX (another ticket).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Choosing Merkle vs linear chaining: Merkle reduces re-computation for fine-grained proofs at the cost of more complex chunking metadata. Initial implementation uses linear hash chaining per ingestion shard with an optional Merkle prototype (see notes).
- Centralized signer vs per-region signer: Per-region KMS keys increase isolation for data residency but complicate signature verification across regions. We will support per-region keys with a key registry in the manifest.
- WORM enforcement: Rely on object lock + retention on S3 where available; for on-prem, provide a write-only endpoint with process-level guarantees and signed attestations.

Acceptance criteria:
1) All admin/action/access/config-change events produced by runtime and console are emitted into the audit producer with a deterministic hash and chain pointer.
2) Exporter produces signed manifests at configurable intervals (default: hourly) and writes to target WORM bucket with retention metadata.
3) Verification CLI validates manifests, signatures, and content for a sample export set; verification run documented in runbook.
4) End-to-end automated test that injects synthetic events, runs exporter, and verifies tamper detection when a payload is intentionally mutated.
5) Docs and runbook updated; PRs merged and smoke-tests passing in staging.

Implementation notes and progress log:
- 2026-02-22: Architecture sync with PM/Trust (Aisha, Omar, Priya). Decided on linear per-shard chaining for MVP to reduce cross-shard coordination. Action: ENG to prototype chain header and manifest schema.
- 2026-02-25: Prototype chain header implemented (ENG branch: feature/audit-chain). Chain header fields: shard_id, sequence_start, sequence_end, prev_chain_hash, chunk_hash, timestamp. Added hashing util (sha256) and deterministic serialization.
- 2026-02-28: KMS integration spike (ENG-11688) complete. Using envelope signing with customer-managed keys for Private installs and Redwood-managed keys for hosted. Key registry added to manifest schema.
- 2026-03-01: Storage sink for WORM implemented in S3 writer with object lock mode and retention metadata. On-prem writer interface sketched; needs additional hardening and attestation.
- 2026-03-03: Verification CLI prototype (go) created; supports public-key retrieval from manifest and rehashing payloads. Basic tests pass locally. CLI repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-verify (WIP).
- 2026-03-05: PR opened for exporter and signer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1892. Reviews requested from @maria and @cheng.

Review feedback (summary):
- Maria (sec): include key rotation metadata and proof-of-previous-signatures in manifest. Action: add prev_key_id and rotation_proof fields.
- Cheng (infra): chunk size tuning required to balance re-download cost vs verification speed. Suggested default chunk size 64MB and ability to tune per-customer.
- Priya (PM): ensure manifest contains residency_tag and customer_id to enforce export placement.

Open tasks (next):
- Add key rotation metadata and implement rotation_proof scheme (assigned Diego).
- Add per-customer residency_tag into manifest writer and double-check bucket access policies (assigned SRE).
- Harden on-prem WORM writer: design attestation message and local immutable store (spike planned for 2026-03-09).
- Extend verification CLI to offline mode and add smoke tests to CI.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for hashing and chain header serialization.
- Integration test that ingests synthetic admin events, runs exporter, uploads to staging WORM bucket, and runs verification CLI.
- Fault-injection test that alters a payload object post-upload and verifies that verification CLI reports tamper.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge MVP to staging behind feature flag.
2) Run end-to-end export+verify for 48h on compliance-staging.
3) Security review and key rotation tabletop exercise.
4) Gradual rollout to hosted customers with high compliance needs, then enable for Private deployments as opt-in.

Monitoring & alerts:
- Exporter failure metric and signature mismatch metric.
- Alert: signature_mismatch_rate > 0 for >5 minutes triggers oncall.

Documentation and audit artifacts:
- Runbook: docs/internal/audit_export_runbook.md
- Manifest schema: docs/internal/audit_manifest_v1.md
- Verification CLI README and usage examples in repo.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Event-level chain headers emitted for all admin/access/config events and visible in staging logs.
2) Hourly signed manifests written to target WORM bucket with retention metadata.
3) Verification CLI reproduces signature and hash checks for a 24h export and fails when content mutated.
4) Security review signed off and runbook published.
notes: Diego to demo verifier to Trust team 2026-03-08. Coordinate with SRE to provision staging WORM buckets with object lock enabled. Ensure CI job can run verification against S3-mock for PR checks.
